bubble-clean.label: Operational Platform / Service Management System

cover.alt: Bubble Clean operational platform project cover

home_copy: An operational web platform for a cleaning company, built to manage clients, properties, staff, scheduled services, payments, before-and-after records, loyalty, referrals, and cleaner routes.
bubble-clean.role: Product strategy, system architecture, full-stack development, interface design, operational workflow design
hero_copy: Bubble Clean started as a simple landing page and admin system. After the first discovery conversation, it became clear that the business needed more than a static website or a backend only the administrator could use.
The result was a self-supporting platform designed around three types of users: admin, client, and cleaner - each with its own role, workflow, and reason to interact with the system.

snapshot.Type: Operational Platform / Service Management System / Client Portal
snapshot.Role: Product strategy, system architecture, full-stack development, interface design, operational workflow design
snapshot.Stack: React, TypeScript, Node.js, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
snapshot.Deliverables: Admin dashboard, client portal, cleaner portal, property management, service scheduling, payment links, service reports, before-and-after photos, loyalty system, referral system, preferred cleaner logic, check-in/check-out, route planning

Context: A cleaning company needed a website and a management system to organize clients, properties, services, employees, and scheduled work.

The initial idea was straightforward: create a landing page and a separate admin area where the business owner could manage the operation. But once the workflow was mapped, the opportunity became much bigger.

Instead of building a system that depended entirely on the administrator, the platform was designed to let clients and cleaners participate directly in the process - creating a more transparent, useful, and scalable experience for everyone involved.
Challenge: The challenge was to move beyond a traditional admin panel.
The company needed a way to manage the operation internally, but also give clients access to their own properties, service history, payments, loyalty rewards, and service records.
Cleaners also needed a practical interface to check in, check out, track work, understand scheduled jobs, view estimated earnings, and follow a route sequence throughout the day.
Solution: I built a multi-role platform with dedicated experiences for admins, clients, and cleaners.

Admins can manage the full operation. Clients can control their properties, view scheduled and completed services, access payment links, review reports, see before-and-after photos, rate services, choose a preferred cleaner, and use loyalty or referral benefits.
Cleaners can access their own portal, check in and out of each property, track service time, view assigned jobs, manage estimated earnings, and use route planning connected to Google Maps.

The platform now supports the business operation, gives clients more control and visibility, and helps cleaners understand their work, schedule, and earning opportunities.

For the company, the system creates a clearer operational structure. For clients, it provides transparency and convenience. For cleaners, it makes the service flow easier to follow and more accountable.

home_copy: A marketplace designed to bring structure, trust, and operational flow to airline miles transactions that used to happen informally through WhatsApp and Telegram groups.
Users can create offers, request quotes, negotiate through chat, complete payments, track wallet activity, and rate each transaction inside one platform.
euquero-milhas.role: Full-stack development, marketplace logic, payment flow, wallet structure, user experience, server configuration
hero_copy: EuQueroMilhas was created to organize airline miles transactions that were happening informally through WhatsApp and Telegram groups in Brazil.

The platform was designed to connect people who buy, sell, or quote airline miles and tickets through a more structured experience - with offers, negotiations, chat, payments, wallet tracking, reports, and user ratings inside one system.

snapshot.Role: Full-stack development, marketplace logic, payment flow, wallet structure, user experience, server configuration
snapshot.Stack: Laravel, MySQL, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Mercado Pago API, CEP API, Airports API, Linux server configuration
snapshot.Deliverables: Marketplace flow, offer listings, quote requests, buy/sell flow, negotiation system, chat, payment flow, wallet, withdrawal request logic, transaction reports, user ratings, external API integrations, Linux server setup

Context: The idea came from a real market behavior: airline miles transactions were often handled inside private groups, informal conversations, and fragmented tools.

Experienced users could negotiate through those channels, but the process was difficult to scale, hard to organize, and not accessible enough for people who did not already understand how airline miles worked.
The opportunity was to turn that informal flow into a platform where users, buyers, sellers, and travel agencies could interact through a more organized and trustworthy process.
Challenge: The main challenge was not only listing offers. The platform needed to support different types of users and different levels of experience.

Some users already knew how to buy and sell miles. Others only wanted to request a quote without having all final travel details. Travel agencies needed a way to estimate values and connect with sellers before having full customer information.
The system also needed to reduce friction and uncertainty by centralizing negotiation, payment, confirmation, wallet tracking, and user reputation.
Solution: I built a marketplace with three main offer segments: quote, buy, and sell.

The quote flow allows users or travel agencies to provide basic trip details, such as passenger count, destination, and travel dates, and receive offers without needing to understand the full airline miles process.
Once a transaction moves forward, users can chat, finalize details, complete payment, track funds, confirm transaction steps, and rate each other after the process.

outcome: EuQueroMilhas transformed an informal group-based process into a structured marketplace experience.

Instead of scattered negotiations across messages, payments, and third-party tools, the platform creates a single place for users to list offers, request quotes, negotiate, complete payments, track funds, and evaluate transactions.
The system supports both experienced airline miles users and people who need a simpler entry point into the process, creating a more organized experience for buyers, sellers, and travel agencies.

cover.alt: PressPlay LMS custom learning platform project cover

home_copy: From a local business website to a custom course platform.

PressPlay LMS was built for a beauty studio that needed more control over how courses were sold, delivered, and experienced - without depending on generic LMS tools or disconnected third-party platforms.
pressplay-lms.role: Custom plugin development, LMS architecture, WooCommerce integration, course experience, interface customization
hero_copy: What started as a simple website for a beauty studio became a custom LMS designed around ownership, flexibility, course sales, student progress, video delivery, and brand experience.
Instead of forcing the business into a generic third-party course platform, I built a custom WordPress plugin integrated with WooCommerce and Vimeo.

snapshot.Type: Custom LMS / WordPress Plugin / WooCommerce Platform
snapshot.Role: Full-stack development, plugin architecture, WooCommerce integration, LMS logic, interface customization
snapshot.Stack: PHP, WordPress Hooks, WooCommerce Hooks, JavaScript, CSS, Vimeo API
snapshot.Deliverables: Custom LMS plugin, course management, teacher management, course categories, included materials, student area, progress tracking, certificates, Vimeo video integration, WooCommerce enrollment flow, custom course pages

Context: A beauty studio in Sao Paulo reached out looking for a website to promote its local business and a way to sell courses based on its professional specialties.

At first, the project looked like a traditional website plus a course area. But once we analyzed the business model, the limitations became clear: the client needed control over the course experience, the visual identity, the purchase flow, and the way students accessed content.
Challenge: Most ready-made course platforms created the same problem: they were either too limited in customization, disconnected from the website experience, or expensive once recurring platform costs were added to payment processing fees.
WordPress LMS plugins were an option, but the ones that could handle the required features depended on premium plans and still did not fully match the client workflow.

The challenge was to create a learning system that felt native to the website, worked with WooCommerce, supported video lessons, tracked student progress, and allowed the studio to manage courses without depending on an external LMS platform.
Solution: I built a custom WordPress plugin that turns the website into a course platform.

The system allows the client to create courses, manage teachers, organize categories, define what is included in each course, customize course pages, deliver video lessons through Vimeo, track student progress, and issue certificates only after completion.

Courses are connected to WooCommerce, which means the purchase flow stays inside the existing commerce structure. When a course is created, the system can also create the related WooCommerce product and use purchase events to generate student enrollment automatically.

outcome: The final result was an owned learning platform built inside the client WordPress ecosystem.
Instead of relying on a disconnected LMS, the studio gained control over course management, student access, video delivery, progress tracking, certificates, and the sales flow through WooCommerce.

PressPlay LMS gave the client something generic tools could not: control - over the course structure, the visual experience, the student journey, the checkout flow, and the way learning content lives inside the brand website.
